title: Genuinely Unextendible Product Bases from Maximum Distance Separable Codes
abstract: The existence of genuinely unextendible product bases (GUPBs), incomplete orthogonal sets of fully product states whose orthogonal complements contain no product vector across any bipartition, has remained an open problem. Here we construct GUPBs for any number $N\geq3$ of parties using classical maximum distance separable (MDS) codes. The MDS property imposes a rigidity on the induced product tiling across every bipartition; combined with Fourier mode deletion and a stopper state, this rigidity enforces genuine unextendibility. Consequently, the orthogonal complement of each GUPB is a genuinely entangled subspace whose normalized projector is invariant under partial transposition across every bipartition, yielding an explicit family of multipartite bound entangled states. We further construct GME witnesses that detect these states even though no fully decomposable witness can do so. Moreover, the resulting indistinguishability persists under arbitrary finite tensor powers and measurements separable across any bipartition. These results establish a direct connection between error-correcting codes and multipartite entanglement and provide an algebraic route to certifying genuinely multipartite bound entanglement.
summary: This work constructs Genuinely Unextendible Product Bases (GUPBs) using mathematical structures derived from Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) error-correcting codes. These bases define complementary subspaces that are proven to host genuinely multipartite bound entangled states. The paper provides both an explicit construction and rigorous tools, like specialized entanglement witnesses, to certify this non-local entanglement.
main_problem: The paper addresses the open problem of constructing Genuinely Unextendible Product Bases (GUPBs) for $N \ge 3$ parties and establishing a deep connection between these bases and multipartite entanglement.
main_result: An explicit family of GUPBs is constructed using classical Maximum Distance Separable (MDS) codes, which in turn yields an algebraic route to certifying genuinely multipartite bound entangled states.
method: The construction relies on the rigidity imposed by MDS codes on product tilings, combined with Fourier mode deletion and a 'stopper' state to prove genuine unextendibility via orthogonality arguments.
model_or_system: The system involves multipartite quantum states in $(\mathbb{C}^{p})^{\otimes N}$, analyzed through orthogonal product bases ($\mathcal{U}_C$) whose complementary subspace is shown to host bound entanglement.
key_observables: GUPBs, genuinely entangled subspaces (GES), GME witnesses, and the discrimination constant $\kappa_{\ell, X|Y}$.
important_parameters: $N \ge 3$ parties; prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $p \ge N^2$; finite tensor powers ($\otimes^\ell$).
main_assumptions: The construction requires the existence of suitable MDS codes and relies on algebraic properties derived from orthogonality relations.
figures_summary: Not specified by notes, but the analysis involves projector operators ($\Pi_G$, $P_U$) and discrimination bounds $\kappa_{\ell, X|Y}$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the GUPB construction using MDS codes (Chunk 1), to proving the entanglement properties of the complementary subspace via orthogonality conditions (Chunk 2), then detailing distinguishability criteria and witnesses (Chunk 3), and finally analyzing stability under tensor products (Chunk 4).
why_interesting: The direct link established between classical error-correcting codes (MDS codes) and certifying genuine multipartite entanglement provides a powerful, algebraic tool for quantum information theory.
